hooks.Video_01_short_1: That 10.5 percent gap is not a rounding error. It is a commercial risk sitting inside your project.
hooks.Video_01_short_2: Here is a number that keeps site managers awake at night: executed 70 percent, accepted 59.5 percent.
hooks.Video_01_short_3: The moment the gap crosses five percent, you escalate. The moment it crosses ten, you stop hiding it in the report.
hooks.Video_02_short_1: Here is the myth: teams believe the curve is a smooth S. The myth is that effort is linear over time.
hooks.Video_02_short_2: Phase two is production. This is where most of the physical progress is measured.
hooks.Video_02_short_3: Why does the last thirty percent of a project take so much longer than the first seventy?
hooks.Video_03_short_1: If your S-curve looks too smooth, it is probably not telling you the truth.
hooks.Video_03_short_2: A real project curve has steps, pauses and corrections. A reported one is usually a drawing.
hooks.Video_03_short_3: BuildTrack keeps the baseline, the earned value and the certificate value in one view so the three checks take seconds.
